doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Algiers places, ball games and Frankie Duson
title: Mooney's trombone, given to Boogerman, and his nine years of baseball
summary: Asked whether he ever played an instrument, Martin says only the kazoo, and that the trombone Boogerman played had been his; he gave it up for baseball in Memphis. He played outfield and caught for nine years.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Cornet or trumpet: choosing and owning horns

blocks.x: Oh, I'm gonna ask Mooney, did you ever play any instrument at all? That's the only thing I ever played for you.
Yeah. Somebody told me they thought you played trombone or something. I had a trombone.

But you never did play. No, the trombone that Booger Man had, that was my trombone. Well, that had been your trombone. That was mine. But you never did learn it. No. I'm crazy but bold. Yeah. And bold time come. I just... Yeah. See my old, my parrain, he was trying to blow a clarinet there. Who there was Robert Williams? Remember Robert Williams? Yeah, that's the guy. Oh yeah, you know, that's E.J. and William in Port Bratel. He had a clarinet. I had the trombone, you know, and when bold time come, I ain't study about no trombone, I give it to Booger. Booger was playing guitar. Booger, Super La, all of them was playing guitar. I had the trombone. And I went on to Memphis to play ball.
If you stayed up there, and I'd come back in high school, well, let's book ahead and try them all.
What'd you play in the ball? What position?
Well, I played outfield, I caught nine years. I caught nine years. I played pretty much all in position.
